# pi-slate

> Quiet focused-first TUI for the Pi coding agent. Adds no new model-facing tools, prompts, or model calls.

Select independent surfaces from the closed set: header, footer, editor, sidebar, tool-cards, transcript. Unselected surfaces receive no setter, patch, watcher, or cleanup write. Fresh missing settings select editor + sidebar + tool-cards, with the sidebar hidden by focused mode. Valid legacy settings without surfaces migrate to all six, preserving appearance. Invalid JSON, unknown surfaces, or bad versions activate nothing and preserve the file.

`/slate surfaces` reports saved and active sets. `/slate surfaces set editor`, `/slate surfaces set header tool-cards`, `/slate surfaces full`, and `/slate surfaces none` save an explicit version-1 array and require `/reload`; appearance remains live. To use only cards, run `/slate surfaces set tool-cards` then `/reload`. Focus/width never enable a disabled sidebar.

Theme and fullscreen remain user preferences, never automatic load actions. `/slate theme default` restores Pi's system default; `/slate theme tokyo-night` selects the bundled Tokyo Night theme. Installation preserves an existing selection. Explicit `/slate theme mocha default` and `/slate style default` retain Catppuccin compatibility. `composerMetadata` replaces the in-memory footer setting; old `footer` files and `/slate footer` remain compatible (both keys are written). The footer surface hides Pi's footer using a zero-row component; composer git branch comes from an editor-only service.

Image handling patches only Slate's editor instance, never Editor.prototype or foreign editors. `/prompts` registers only with editor; `/exit` always. Tool-cards preserves native execution outside TUI and native model-facing results; grouped reads and highlighted diffs are rendering only. No stock-notice deletion.

Chrome is last-writer-wins; tools are first-registration-wins, with losses reported and no repair engine. Sidebar/transcript use a namespaced zero-row below-editor TUI handle, need a compatible fullscreen host, and warn rather than forcing fullscreen or overlaying. The sidebar yields to a replaced root. Shutdown disposes local resources without clearing successor slots; `/reload` resets chrome because header/footer ownership getters are unavailable.

Observed TUI thinking adds elapsed seconds and available token rate to the composer-edge working word (`Pondering · 7s · ↑↓42`). Native thinking visibility, streaming labels, and toggles remain unchanged; per-message settled durations await a host API.

Claude Code-style tool cards are the default with tool-cards selected; `toolStyle: "default"` in pi-slate.json plus /reload restores Slate's original cards. Uses Pi registerToolRenderer (tested 1.3.0), compact status/args/result/duration/timeout/diff rows and scoped consecutive-tool trees on compatible fullscreen hosts. No tool re-registration for styling, global prototype patches, session replay or extra timers. Legacy read grouper is disabled in this mode. Expanded original renderers/state, native thinking visibility and schemas remain intact; images, assistant text, unsupported tools and visible thoughts break groups. Older hosts keep default cards with a warning.

Highlighted diffs use responsive split edits, unified writes, and character-level emphasis. They follow `/slate theme`. Native model-facing results are preserved; bounded write patches are stored in TUI result details for session restore.

Header uses the stock Pi mark plus version, model, session dir as ~/<name>, and an optional update hairline. Composer keeps project/branch on the bottom left, focused cost/resources on the top edge, and ctx before model on the bottom right, with square corners matching the fully bordered sidebar. Completed turns add a UI-only elapsed-time receipt with local finish time (Worked for 54s • 09:37). Image placeholders are a single caret object. The rail starts with a live session title in bold theme accent color (click copies the full plain-text title; width-aware ellipsis only affects painting; unnamed sessions leave a blank row), followed by Session <short-id> · PID <pid> (click copies the full ID). Automatic/manual renames update the title through session_info_changed, and /slate session includes the full title. The remaining rail shows context, a merged tokens/cost/rate occupancy line, left-lane Cached/Uncached and right-lane value-first In/Out rows, folded MCP/Skills/Prompts (Enabled/Loaded counts, MCP error counts in red), and live background shells. Commands stay behind / and /slate session commands. Empty task/image shelves disappear. Below 100 columns or 30 rows the rail hides without changing preferences; focused cost/resources, project/branch, and context/model return to the composer without duplicating cost. Pin/inspection and session/root ownership protections remain intact.

## Documentation

- [README](README.md): install, features, commands (`/exit` aliases `/quit`), themes, composer keys
- [Extension entry](extensions/pi-slate/index.ts): selected-surface installers and commands
- [Surfaces](extensions/pi-slate/surfaces.ts): closed enum, parsing, migration
- [Diff](extensions/pi-slate/diff.ts): edit/write rendering
- [Read groups](extensions/pi-slate/read-group.ts): consecutive-read compaction
- [Tool style](extensions/pi-slate/tool-style.ts): presentation-only compact cards
- [Tool groups](extensions/pi-slate/tool-groups.ts): scoped chat-instance trees and native mouse routing
- [Thinking status](extensions/pi-slate/thinking-fold.ts): live composer timing, native transcript fallback
- [Tokyo Night theme](themes/tokyo-night.json): bundled explicit theme choice
- [Black Metal theme](themes/black-metal.json): optional theme, not an install default
- [Package manifest](package.json): `npm:pi-slate`
